correctness.rationale: Reflection splits the 2m-vertex weighted path Laplacian into irreducible Jacobi matrices N_m and N_m+2w e_me_mᵀ. Their spectra are simple and disjoint for w>0 by final-coordinate recurrence. PBH detects zeros of sensor coordinate. Neumann cosine eigenvectors vanish at j iff gcd(m,2j-1)>1; antisymmetric zeros have θ=(2r-1)π/(2j-1) with 1≤r<j, and the terminal boundary equation gives the exact positive W_r with nonzero denominator. Conversely any such W_r yields a nonzero zero-sensor eigenvector. Periodicity m↦m+(2j-1) changes numerator and denominator signs together. For j=2, residues m mod3 give all weights / {1/2} / empty; simple spectrum makes the unobservable dimension one. Independent 390 numerical eigenvector zero tests agree; they are not proof for unbounded m and real w.
residual_risks: Ideal noiseless state observability, not Gramian conditioning.
Unit weights except central positive edge; combinatorial not normalized Laplacian.

value.rationale: A natural one-defective-edge path is the simplest weighted perturbation of a graph signal system; the result completely identifies all positive conductances at which a specified single interior sensor fails, with a striking exact periodic residue law and exact nullspace multiplicity. Useful in sensor placement and fragility analysis, not just endpoint textbook controllability.

limitations: w strictly positive, j in reflected half, 2m vertices m≥2.
